clue.text: Dodgy download offered by the French: it'll infect the others

parts.note: dodgy means bad or suspect
an app is a piece of software you download
le is a French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A warning that a suspicious download will spread a virus to everyone else's devices.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says one bad apple spoils the barrel, which is why the definition talks of infecting the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a single corrupt member of a group whose influence spreads rot to the rest, from the proverb about fruit in a barrel.

clue.text: Rabbit on bundle containing books

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a bale is a tied bundle, as of hay
B is the abbreviation for book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a parcel of books in a rambling way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit on' is British slang for talking at length; the books go inside the bale: BA-BB-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly, and to babble is likewise to talk foolishly without pause.

clue.text: Spicy madras produces sensations

indicators.note: something spicy has been heated up and stirred, so the following word gets its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; madras is a hot curry

explanation.surface: A hot curry creates a stir of feelings in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensations in the sense of exciting, sensational events or scenes, which is what dramas are in everyday speech.

clue.text: Aromatic oil, dressing on distilled coulis

parts.note: a patch is a dressing put over a wound

indicators.note: distilling boils off the outside and keeps the essence, so only the inner letters of the word stay

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A recipe step: pour dressing over a reduced fruit sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a kitchen scene, but the dressing is a bandage, not a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is a heavy fragrant essential oil from an Asian plant, used in perfumes and incense.

clue.text: Symbol for 'toilet' shiftily excluding female!

indicators.note: shiftily suggests letters moving about deviously, so the remaining fodder gets rearranged
excluding means leaving out, and female is the usual abbreviation F, so that letter goes

parts.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: A sign on a lavatory door that keeps women out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a gents' toilet sign does exclude females.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy, childish euphemism for a men's lavatory, which naturally keeps out women, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: 'Unopposed vacuous tycoon' describes president squandering billions

indicators.note: to describe a figure is to draw round it, so one piece goes around the other
vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps only its two ends

parts.note: only the first and last letters

indicators.note: squandering means losing, and billions is abbreviated B, so that letter is thrown away

parts.note: Barack Obama, US president

explanation.surface: A headline jibe at an empty-headed tycoon president winning unopposed while wasting money.
explanation.walkthrough: Obama minus B gives OAMA, which sits between T and N.
explanation.definitionFit: If a group agrees to a man, every single member is in favour, so the proposal meets no opposition.

clue.text: Live with Dyson Airblade missing parts

indicators.note: missing parts means the phrase is shown with its ends cut away, leaving a run of letters from inside

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Living with a hand-dryer that is missing some of its components.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dyson Airblade is a brand of hand dryer found in public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast that is live is being transmitted as it happens, which is what being on air means.

clue.text: Political figure seen at local recycling in 2010

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: 2010 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician photographed at the neighbourhood recycling centre a few years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The year 2010 must be read as Roman numerals, a common crossword convention, rather than as a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm X was the American Black nationalist leader and activist of the 1950s and 1960s.

clue.text: Putting me in post dodgily?

indicators.note: dodgily means in an underhand, irregular way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether their appointment to a job was a crooked favour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the rearranged letters, and a description of a relative wangling a job for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouritism shown to relatives or friends, especially giving them jobs, which is a dodgy way of getting someone appointed.

clue.text: US blogger, lib, is feeble wimp

indicators.note: feeble suggests something weak that falls apart, so the preceding letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling an American liberal blogger weak and cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big girl's blouse' is a British insult for a weak, unmanly person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang insult for a weak, cowardly or oversensitive man, in other words a weakling or sissy.

clue.text: Sandwich sandwiches fizz and 'fudge!'

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to put it between two outer layers

parts.note: a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A lunch order: a sandwich, some fizzy wine, and fudge for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fudge' looks like the sweet on the menu, but it is a mild stand-in for a swear word. Asti is Italian sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance used in place of stronger swearing.

clue.text: What you get if a plan's ill-conceived?

definitions.text: What you get if a plan's ill-conceived?

indicators.note: ill-conceived means badly formed, so the letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what happens when a scheme is badly thought out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a botched plan leaves you flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap means being agitated and panicky, the state a poorly thought-out scheme tends to leave you in.

clue.text: Film-maker, vile creature, changing sides

indicators.note: sides are left and right, so changing sides swaps the letter for one into the letter for the other

parts.note: a cockroach, often called a roach

explanation.surface: A film director dismissed as a loathsome turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left). Ken Loach is a British director of gritty social-realist films.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Loach is a celebrated British director known for films such as Kes and I, Daniel Blake.

clue.text: Boozy yob's unexpectedly got allure

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters coming out in a surprising new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken hooligan has surprisingly become attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British word for a rowdy young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: British term for a young man who drinks heavily and then behaves rowdily or aggressively in public.

clue.text: Masseuse pounds foot, gives blessing

parts.note: someone who rubs you
to stamp is to bring a foot down hard

explanation.surface: A masseuse pummels a client's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp a proposal is to approve it automatically, giving official sanction without real scrutiny.

clue.text: Kicks back and captures man alive in bingo hall

parts.note: to take a piece or a city is to capture it
bingo callers say 'man alive' for the number five

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes, then grabs a winning number at a bingo game.
explanation.walkthrough: Bingo callers use rhyming nicknames for numbers: 'man alive, number five'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking five means having a short rest break, which is relaxing or chilling out for a moment.

clue.text: Bureaucrats in charge fenced in by tenders

indicators.note: fenced in by means enclosed on all sides by the next piece

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer
the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Officials in charge are hemmed in by competing bids.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenders here are formal bids for a contract, not boats or carers.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers are officials holding posts in an organisation, a looser synonym for administrators or bureaucrats.

clue.text: Town in Belgium? Absolutely

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
'right on' is an exclamation of hearty agreement

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a place is in Belgium and gets a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question invites a Belgian town; it is the English seaside resort on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast, a town for most of its history before gaining city status.

clue.text: So far, Skype IT malfunctioning? Oh, come on

indicators.note: malfunctioning means not working properly, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated user whose video call software keeps failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exasperated exclamations of impatience or disbelief at something annoying.

clue.text: Ended the call, being anxious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put the phone down
second meaning: neurotically worried about something

explanation.surface: Someone finished a phone call because they were nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means terminated a telephone conversation, and the adjective means emotionally preoccupied or neurotic.

clue.text: Romantic figure: 'Cold? I'll give you a lift'

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
'hop in' is what a driver says when offering a lift

explanation.surface: A dashing hero offers a shivering stranger a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic figure' suggests a heartthrob; it means a composer of the Romantic era.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was a Polish composer and pianist, a leading figure of the nineteenth-century Romantic movement in music.

clue.text: More-or-less learning to fly across England

indicators.note: across means stretching over and around the other piece
to fly means to scatter, so the letters fly apart and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for England

explanation.surface: Roughly speaking, someone is taking flying lessons over England.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means broadly or as a rule, in the main, which is roughly what more or less conveys.

clue.text: Assassin in Japan's concealed?

indicators.note: concealed means tucked away inside the words just before it

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A question about a Japanese killer lurking unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a ninja is a hidden Japanese assassin, and it is hidden in the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert agents of feudal Japan, trained in stealth and assassination, famous for staying out of sight.

clue.text: Shout out to Antarctica

definitions.note: Antarctica is a place, the answer a direction or region; it stands for the far south

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sending greetings to the people at a polar research station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shout out' reads as a greeting, but out is the anagram signal on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica is the continent at the very bottom of the globe, the furthest point of the southern direction.

clue.text: Consume slice of meat in toastie

indicators.note: a slice of means a section cut from within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Instructions to eat a piece of the filling in a toasted sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: A toastie is a British toasted sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into something is to use up or gradually wear away part of it, such as savings or time.

clue.text: Exhausting American in grump regularly

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States
taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A tiring American who is always in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausting a supply means depleting it completely, so nothing of it remains.

clue.text: Bronze: tin containing uranium, nitrogen and tantalum

indicators.note: containing means holding the following pieces inside

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
chemical symbol
chemical symbol
chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A metallurgist's recipe for an alloy of several elements.
explanation.walkthrough: Bronze looks like the alloy, matching the chemistry; it is skin colour. S-UNTA-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronzed complexion is a skin colour darkened by exposure to sunshine.

clue.text: Queen pursues 'favourite' to criticise 'eternal youth'

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so the first piece follows the second

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
Elizabeth Regina
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: The monarch goes after her favourite courtier to attack the cult of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's character is the boy who never grows up, so his name is used for a perpetually youthful person.
